en: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us; (H) and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us—both of them from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, with this chain of transmission, and he said: "just as an animal gives birth to an animal," and he did not mention "whole/intact (jam'a')."

Hajib ibn al-Walid narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Harb narrated to us, from al-Zubaydi, from al-Zuhri: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab informed me, from Abu Hurayrah, that he used to say: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "There is no newborn except that he is born upon the fitrah (natural disposition), and then his parents make him a Jew, a Christian, or a Magian, just as an animal gives birth to a whole/intact animal: do you perceive in it any that is mutilated?" Then Abu Hurayrah would say: And recite if you wish: {the natural disposition of Allah upon which He has created mankind; no change should there be in the creation of Allah} to the end of the verse.

Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to us: Abu Hisham al-Makhzumi informed us: Wuhayb narrated to us: Suhayl ibn Abi Salih narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "Decreed for the son of Adam is his share of fornication, which he will inevitably attain: the fornication of the eyes is looking, the fornication of the ears is listening, the fornication of the tongue is speech, the fornication of the hand is seizing, and the fornication of the leg is stepping; the heart longs and desires, and the private part either confirms that or denies it."

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us—and the wording is Ishaq's—they said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar narrated to us, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: I have not seen anything that resembles minor faults (al-lamam) more than what Abu Hurayrah said, that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, Allah has decreed for the son of Adam his share of fornication, which he will inevitably attain: the fornication of the eyes is looking, the fornication of the tongue is speaking, the soul wishes and desires, and the private part either confirms that or denies it." 'Abd said in his narration: Ibn Tawus, from his father: I heard Ibn 'Abbas.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, they said: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ziyad ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn 'Abbad ibn Ja'far al-Makhzumi, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The polytheists of Quraysh came disputing with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) concerning the divine decree (al-qadr), so there was revealed: {The Day they are dragged into the Fire on their faces [it will be said], "Taste the touch of Saqar." Indeed, all things We created with predestination.}

'Abd al-A'la ibn Hammad narrated to me, saying: I read to Malik ibn Anas; (H) and Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Malik, in what was read to him, from Ziyad ibn Sa'd, from 'Amr ibn Muslim, from Tawus, that he said: I met people from the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: "Everything is by divine decree (qadar)." He said: And I heard 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Everything is by divine decree, even helplessness and shrewdness, or shrewdness and helplessness."

Zuhayr ibn Harb and Ibn Numayr narrated to me, both from al-Muqri'; Zuhayr said: 'Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Muqri' narrated to us, saying: Haywah narrated to us: Abu Hani' informed me that he heard Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli say that he heard 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As say that he heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: "Indeed, all the hearts of the children of Adam are between two fingers of the fingers of the Most Merciful, like a single heart; He turns it wherever He wills." Then the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "O Allah, Turner of the hearts, turn our hearts towards Your obedience."

Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us: al-Muqri' narrated to us: Haywah narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn Sahl al-Tamimi narrated to me: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us: Nafi'—meaning Ibn Yazid—informed us, both from Abu Hani', with this chain of transmission, the like of it, except that they did not mention: "and His Throne was over the water."

Abu al-Tahir Ahmad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Abdillah ibn 'Amr ibn Sarh narrated to me: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: Abu Hani' al-Khawlani informed me, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: "Allah wrote the decrees of creation fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth—he said: and His Throne was over the water."

And Muhammad ibn Minhal al-Darir narrated to us: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us: Hisham ibn Hassan narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of their hadith.

And Ibn Rafi' narrated to us: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), with the meaning of their hadith.

'Amr al-Naqid narrated to me: Ayyub ibn al-Najjar al-Yamami narrated to us: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir narrated to us, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace); (H)

Zuhayr ibn Harb and Ibn Hatim narrated to me, they said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: my father narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, from Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Adam and Moses debated. Moses said to him: 'You are Adam whom your sin expelled from Paradise.' Adam said to him: 'You are Moses whom Allah chose with His message and with His speech, yet you blame me for a matter that was decreed for me before I was created?' Thus Adam overcame Moses in debate."

Ishaq ibn Musa ibn 'Abdillah ibn Musa ibn 'Abdillah ibn Yazid al-Ansari narrated to us: Anas ibn 'Iyad narrated to us: al-Harith ibn Abi Dhubab narrated to me, from Yazid—who is Ibn Hurmuz—and 'Abd al-Rahman al-A'raj, they said: We heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Adam and Moses (peace be upon them) debated before their Lord, and Adam overcame Moses in debate. Moses said: 'You are Adam whom Allah created with His hand, breathed into you of His spirit, made His angels prostrate to you, and settled you in His Paradise, yet you brought mankind down by your sin to the earth.' Adam said: 'You are Moses whom Allah chose with His message and with His speech, gave you the Tablets containing the explanation of all things, and brought you near in private communion. By how much did you find that Allah wrote the Torah before I was created?' Moses said: 'By forty years.' Adam said: 'Did you find in it: {and Adam disobeyed his Lord and went astray}?' He said: 'Yes.' Adam said: 'Do you then blame me for having done an action that Allah wrote upon me that I would do forty years before He created me?'" The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Thus Adam overcame Moses in debate."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Malik ibn Anas, in what was read to him, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Adam and Moses debated, and Adam overcame Moses in debate. Moses said to him: 'You are Adam who led the people astray and brought them out of Paradise.' Adam said: 'You are the one to whom Allah gave knowledge of everything and chose above the people with His message.' He said: 'Yes.' Adam said: 'Then do you blame me for a matter that was decreed upon me before I was created?'"

Muhammad ibn Hatim, Ibrahim ibn Dinar, Ibn Abi 'Umar al-Makki, and Ahmad ibn 'Abdah al-Dabbi all narrated to me from Ibn 'Uyaynah—and the wording is Ibn Hatim's and Ibn Dinar's—they said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from 'Amr, from Tawus, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Adam and Moses debated. Moses said: 'O Adam, you are our father, you brought us disappointment and brought us out of Paradise.' Adam said to him: 'You are Moses; Allah chose you with His speech and inscribed for you with His hand. Do you blame me for a matter that Allah decreed upon me forty years before He created me?'" The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "So Adam overcame Moses in debate; so Adam overcame Moses in debate." And in the hadith of Ibn Abi 'Umar and Ibn 'Abdah, one of them said: "inscribed (khatta)," and the other said: "wrote the Torah for you with His hand."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: 'Abd al-'Aziz—meaning Ibn Muhammad—narrated to us, from al-'Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, a man may do the deeds of the people of Paradise for a long time, then his deeds are sealed with the deeds of the people of the Fire; and indeed, a man may do the deeds of the people of the Fire for a long time, then his deeds are sealed with the deeds of the people of Paradise."

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali narrated to us: 'Uthman ibn 'Umar narrated to us: 'Azrah ibn Thabit narrated to us, from Yahya ibn 'Uqayl, from Yahya ibn Ya'mur, from Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali, who said: 'Imran ibn al-Husayn said to me: "Have you considered what people do today and strive in: is it something that has been decreed for them and passed for them from a destiny that preceded, or is it concerning what they face in the future of what their Prophet brought them and by which the proof was established against them?" I said: "Rather, it is something decreed for them and passed for them." He said: "Would that not then be an injustice?" He said: I was terrified by that with a severe fright, and I said: "Everything is the creation of Allah and the possession of His hand; He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned." He said to me: "May Allah have mercy on you! I only intended by what I asked you to test your intellect. Indeed, two men from Muzaynah came to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, have you considered what people do today and strive in: is it something that has been decreed for them and passed concerning them from a destiny that preceded, or is it concerning what they face in the future of what their Prophet brought them and by which the proof was established against them?' He said: 'No, rather it is something decreed for them and passed concerning them, and the confirmation of that is in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: {And [by] the soul and He who proportioned it * And inspired it [with discernment of] its wickedness and its righteousness.}'"

Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us: 'Abd al-Warith narrated to us; (H) and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Zuhayr ibn Harb, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, and Ibn Numayr narrated to us from Ibn 'Ulayyah; (H) and Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Ja'far ibn Sulayman informed us; (H) and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us—all of them from Yazid al-Rishk, in this chain of transmission, with the meaning of Hammad's hadith. And in the hadith of 'Abd al-Warith: he said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah..."

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Hammad ibn Zayd informed us, from Yazid al-Duba'i: Mutarrif narrated to us, from 'Imran ibn Husayn, who said: It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, are the people of Paradise known from the people of the Fire?" He said: He said: "Yes." He said: It was said: "Then why do workers strive?" He said: "Everyone is facilitated for that for which he was created."

Abu al-Tahir narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir ibn 'Abdillah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), with this meaning, and in it: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Every worker is facilitated for his work."

Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us: Zuhayr narrated to us: Abu al-Zubayr narrated to us; (H) and Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Abu Khaythamah informed us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: Suraqah ibn Malik ibn Ju'shum came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, explain our religion to us as if we were created just now. In what is deeds done today: is it in that which the pens have dried upon and the decrees have run with, or in what we face in the future?" He said: "No, rather in that which the pens have dried upon and the decrees have run with." He said: "Then why do deeds?" Zuhayr said: Then Abu al-Zubayr said something I did not understand, so I asked what he said, and he said: "Work, for everyone is facilitated."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Mansur and al-A'mash, that they both heard Sa'd ibn 'Ubaydah narrating it from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from 'Ali, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of it.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Zuhayr ibn Harb, and Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, they said: Waki' narrated to us; (H) and Ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us: al-A'mash narrated to us; (H) and Abu Kurayb narrated to us—and the wording is his: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us: al-A'mash narrated to us, from Sa'd ibn 'Ubaydah, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from 'Ali, who said: One day the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was sitting with a stick in his hand scraping the ground with it. He raised his head and said: "There is not a soul among you but its dwelling in Paradise and the Fire is already known." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, then why should we strive? Should we not just rely upon it?" He said: "No, strive, for everyone is facilitated for that for which he was created." Then he recited: {As for he who gives and fears Allah * And believes in the best [reward]} up to His words: {We will ease him toward difficulty.}

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Hannad ibn al-Sari narrated to us, they said: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Mansur, with this chain of transmission, in its meaning, and he said: "so he took a stick," and did not say: "a small staff (mikhsarah)." And Ibn Abi Shaybah said in his hadith from Abu al-Ahwas: "Then the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) recited..."

'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah, Zuhayr ibn Harb, and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—and the wording is Zuhayr's; Ishaq said: "informed us" and the other two said: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Sa'd ibn 'Ubaydah, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'Ali, who said: We were at a funeral in Baqi' al-Gharqad when the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) came to us. He sat down and we sat around him. He had a small staff with him, so he bowed his head and began scratching the ground with his staff. Then he said: "There is no one among you, no created soul, but Allah has written its place in Paradise and the Fire, and has written it as either wretched or blessed." He said: A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, should we not then rely upon our decree and abandon deeds?" He said: "Whoever is of the people of bliss will turn toward the deeds of the people of bliss, and whoever is of the people of misery will turn toward the deeds of the people of misery." Then he said: "Strive, for everyone is facilitated: as for the people of bliss, they are facilitated for the deeds of the people of bliss; and as for the people of misery, they are facilitated for the deeds of the people of misery." Then he recited: {As for he who gives and fears Allah * And believes in the best [reward] * We will ease him toward ease * But as for he who withholds and considers himself free of need * And denies the best [reward] * We will ease him toward difficulty.}

Abu Kamil Fudayl ibn Husayn al-Jahdari narrated to me: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us: 'Ubaydullah ibn Abi Bakr narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik, elevating the hadith, that he said: "Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has appointed an angel over the womb, who says: 'O Lord, a drop of fluid (nutfah)? O Lord, a clinging clot ('alaqah)? O Lord, a lump of flesh (mudghah)?' Then when Allah wills to decree a creation—he said—the angel says: 'O Lord, male or female? Wretched or blessed? What is the provision? What is the lifespan?' So that is written accordingly in his mother's womb."

'Abd al-Warith ibn 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us: my father narrated to me: Rabi'ah ibn Kulthum narrated to us: my father Kulthum narrated to me, from Abu al-Tufayl, from Hudhayfah ibn Asid al-Ghifari, the companion of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), elevating the hadith to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace): "Indeed, an angel is appointed over the womb; when Allah wills to create something by Allah's leave after forty-some nights..." then he mentioned the like of their hadith.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Khalaf narrated to me: Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr narrated to us: Zuhayr Abu Khaythamah narrated to us: 'Abdullah ibn 'Ata' narrated to me that 'Ikrimah ibn Khalid narrated to him that Abu al-Tufayl narrated to him, saying: I entered upon Abu Sarihah Hudhayfah ibn Asid al-Ghifari, and he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) with these two ears of mine saying: "Indeed, the drop of fluid (nutfah) rests in the womb for forty nights, then the angel takes form over it"—Zuhayr said: I think he said: the one who forms it—"and says: 'O Lord, male or female?' And Allah makes it male or female. Then he says: 'O Lord, sound/well-formed or deformed?' And Allah makes it well-formed or deformed. Then he says: 'O Lord, what is its provision? What is its lifespan? What is its character?' Then Allah makes it wretched or blessed."

Ahmad ibn 'Uthman al-Nawfali narrated to us: Abu 'Asim informed us: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us: Abu al-Zubayr informed me that Abu al-Tufayl informed him that he heard 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud saying... and he pursued the hadith with the like of the hadith of 'Amr ibn al-Harith.
